(p-195)
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surah At-Taghabun (The Mutual Loss and Gain)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, to Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things competent.﴾

The meaning of tasbih (glorification of Allah, declaring Him free from every imperfection) and the significance of "whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth" have already been discussed at the beginning of Surah al-Hashr and Surah al-Hadid. This surah is the last of the surahs that open with tasbih. The verb here is in the present tense (al-mudari'), which indicates renewal and continuous occurrence. The verse concludes by attributing to Allah the perfect qualities through His saying: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things competent﴾, to indicate that dominion belongs to Allah alone, without partner; His command is executed over it, His judgment prevails in it, and the reins of His affairs are in His hand, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is over all things competent﴾ [al-Mulk: 1].

And like His saying in Surah Ya-Sin: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is. So exalted is He in whose hand is the realm of all things, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82-83].

And from His power over all things, and His disposing of the affairs of His dominion as He wills, is that He made the whole world glorify Him with His praise, executing a wisdom within it, as in His saying: ﴿To Him belongs praise in the first and the last, and to Him belongs judgment, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Qasas: 70]. Thus He combined praise and judgment together, for the majesty of His power and the perfection of His attributes.

The commentator al-Shinqiti (may God have mercy on us and him) said in *Mudhakkirat al-Dirasa*: The meaning is that God is the One who created you, and He decreed disbelief for some of you and faith for others. Then after that He guides each to what He has decreed for him, as He said: ﴿And He who decreed and then guided﴾ [Al-A'la: 3]. He makes the disbeliever easy toward the work of disbelief, and makes the believer easy toward the work of faith, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for." End of quotation.

It is well known that this text is a point of difficulty for the Qadariyya (those who deny divine predestination) and the Jabriyya (those who hold that man has no choice). Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah, the orthodox majority) believe that all things occur by the decree and will of God. Ibn Taymiyya said in *al-Aqida al-Wasitiyya*: The People of the Sunnah are a middle position between the view that the servant is compelled in his actions and has no choice, like a leaf in the wind, and the view that the servant creates his own act and does what he wills by his own will.

The People of the Sunnah say according to the words of God: ﴿For whoever among you wills to take a straight path. But you do not will unless God wills, Lord of the worlds﴾ [At-Takwir: 29].

Al-Qurtubi mentioned the views of the two groups of scholars, and each group has what it cited as evidence. The first is from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God created Pharaoh in his mother's womb as a disbeliever, and created Yahya ibn Zakariyya in his mother's womb as a believer."

This is consistent with what is in the Sahih from the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Indeed, one of you acts with the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and it only a cubit or a fathom, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he acts with the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it. And indeed, one of you acts with the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is between him and it only a cubit or a fathom, and then the Decree overtakes him, and he acts with the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it."

He said: Our scholars said: The eternal knowledge (al-'ilm al-azali) has related to every object of knowledge, so what He knew and willed and decreed takes place.

The second view: What came in the saying of the scholars: Some scholars said: God created the creation, then they disbelieved and believed. They said: The completion of the speech is: ﴿He is the One who created you﴾, then He described them, saying: ﴿So among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾.

And like His saying: ﴿And God created every creature from water; so among them is one that walks on its belly﴾ [An-Nur: 45]. They said: God created them, and walking is their action.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl chose this view, saying: Because if He had created them as disbelievers and believers, He would not have described them by their own actions. They argued with the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Every child is born upon the fitra (natural disposition)," and the hadith continues. End of quotation.

Considering these two statements, we find the following:

First: The analogy in the second statement is not sound, because describing animals while they walk is not a description of an action; it is rather part of God's creation of them, and there was no action from them in that.

Second: What each group cited from the two hadiths does not conflict. The first hadith, "Indeed one of you acts," explains the final destination and outcome, according to the eternal knowledge and the decree of will.

The second hadith explains the origin of a person's existence in this world, that he is born upon the fitra when he is born. As for his final destination, it is according to what God has decreed for him.

Al-Qurtubi quoted a statement by al-Zajjaj and said of it: It is the best of the views. Its text is: God created the disbeliever, and his disbelief is an action of his and an acquisition (kasb), although God is the Creator of disbelief. He created the believer, and his faith is an action of his and an acquisition, although God is the Creator of faith. The disbeliever disbelieves and chooses disbelief after God created him, because God decreed that for him and knew it of him, since the existence of what contradicts the decree is incapacity, and the existence of what contradicts the known is ignorance.

Al-Qurtubi said: This is the best of the views, and it is the view held by the majority of the Ummah. End of quotation.

Perhaps what supports al-Zajjaj's view is His saying: ﴿And God created you and what you do﴾ [As-Saffat: 96].

This is the summary of what the scholars of tafsir said. This position, as we have previously stated, is a point of difficulty concerning decree and compulsion, and feet have slipped in it and understandings have gone astray. By reflecting on the text and the texts surrounding it in the context before and after it, we find the correct answer and the sound direction. That begins with His saying: ﴿To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent﴾.

The fact that dominion belongs to Him means that nothing occurs in His dominion except what He wills, and His being over all things competent means that He does in His dominion what He wills.

Then He said: ﴿He is the One who created you; so among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer. And God is Seeing of what you do﴾.

Then there came after it

﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth, and fashioned you and made your forms good, and to Him is the final return.﴾ ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose, and Allah is Knower of what is within the breasts.﴾

The creation of the heavens and the earth, and the creation of man in the best form, are two signs among the signs that point to the resurrection (al-ba'th), as He said in the first: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir: 57].

He said in the second: ﴿Say: He will give them life who brought them into being the first time, and He is Knower of every creation﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79].

(p-198) Therefore after them comes His saying: ﴿And to Him is the final return.﴾

That is: after death and resurrection. It is as if He is saying to them: He is the One who created you and created for you signs of His power to resurrect you. Among these is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and among them is your creation and your fashioning in the finest form. So the required response to this is belief in His power to resurrect you after death, and consequently your belief in what follows resurrection, of reckoning, recompense, Paradise and Hellfire. But among you there is a disbeliever and among you a believer.

After the mention of the nations before them and the description of their conditions, there came the refutation of the disbelievers' claim about resurrection and the oath affirming its occurrence in His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed of what you did, and that is easy for Allah﴾ [al-Taghabun: 7]. This is because the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. This interpretation is supported by His saying in Surat al-Insan: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning? Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture that We may try him, and We made him hearing and seeing. Indeed, We guided him to the way, be he grateful or be he ungrateful﴾ [al-Insan: 1–3].

His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture﴾ is like His saying ﴿It is He who created you﴾ [al-Taghabun: 2].

Then He said: ﴿And made him hearing and seeing﴾, and these are the two faculties of perception and reflection. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾, along with his readiness to accept or reject.

His saying ﴿be he grateful or be he ungrateful﴾ is like His saying here: ﴿among you a disbeliever and among you a believer﴾ [al-Taghabun: 2], meaning after reflection and consideration, and after being guided to the way through revelation (wahy). Therefore in this context of this surah comes: ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the light that We have sent down﴾ [al-Taghabun: 8].

From all that has preceded, it becomes clear to us in general that Allah created man from a sperm-drop, then gave him hearing and sight, and set up the proofs of His existence and His power to resurrect the dead, and consequently to recompense them for their deeds. He sent His messengers to him and guided him to the two paths. Then, after all that, he is either grateful or ungrateful. And if a person in this world were to argue by divine decree (al-qadar), it would be said to him: Do you have knowledge of what Allah has decreed concerning you in His knowledge, or has Allah commanded you, forbidden you, and explained the path to you?

(p-199) In any case, the matter of divine decree (al-qadar) is among the most dangerous and most obscure of questions. As ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Al-qadar is the secret of Allah in His creation."

The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "When the decree (al-qadar) is mentioned, hold back." But it is incumbent upon the Muslim to reflect on what Allah has sent down of revelation and what He has sent of messengers.

The most important aspect of the matter is that affairs proceed according to the will of Allah. A practical event has occurred in the battle of Badr that clarifies the reality of divine decree and displays the greatest lessons, in His saying: ﴿When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few. And had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage and disputed about the matter, but Allah saved you. Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾ [al-Anfal: 43].

So He, the Exalted, is the One who saved them from the causes of dispute and cowardice, in accordance with His knowledge of what is within the breasts.

Then He said: ﴿And when He showed them to you as few when you met, and made you seem few in their eyes, so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done. And to Allah all matters are returned﴾ [al-Anfal: 44]. He carried out the causes according to the requirement of His will, making each of the two groups seem few in the eyes of the other, so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was already fulfilled in His foreknowledge. Then He stated the ultimate end: ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾, and knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 64, verse 6:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said, "Shall mere humans guide us?" So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was self-sufficient. And Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.﴾

In this verse there is a denunciation by the disbelievers of the idea that the one who guides them should be a human being rather than an angel, as the Exalted said: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:94], and His saying: ﴿"Shall we follow a single human being from among us?"﴾ [al-Qamar 54:24].

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, said in his study notes (Mudhakkirat al-Dirasa): This false doubt of theirs, Allah refuted in many verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾ [al-An'am 6:9];

• His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you except men﴾ [Yusuf 12:109], meaning: not angels;

• His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan 25:20], etc.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was self-sufficient. And Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.﴾

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already discussed this in his commentary on His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And pilgrimage to the House is a duty upon mankind to Allah﴾ (p. 200), up to His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:97].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 64, verse 7:

His saying, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on us and on him: ﴿Those who disbelieved claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that is easy for Allah."﴾

The Shaykh (may Allah the Exalted have mercy on us and on him) said: That is, the disbelievers claimed that they would not be resurrected, saying: "Indeed, decayed bones will not be brought back to life." So say to them, O Prophet of Allah: "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected." Here, "bala" (بلى, "yes") is a particle that comes for one of two meanings. The first is the rejection of a negation, as it is here.

The second is the answer to an interrogative preceded by a negation, such as His saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord? They said, "Yes"﴾ [al-A'raf: 172]. As for His saying, "by my Lord," it is an oath by the Lord concerning the resurrection, which is the bringing back to life after death. He swore by Him concerning it in the Qur'an three times. The first is this one.

The second is His saying: ﴿And they ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is true."﴾ [Yunus: 53].

The third is His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you."﴾ [Saba': 3]. End of quotation.

As for His saying, ﴿then you will surely be informed of what you did﴾, Allah the Exalted explained it with His saying: ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird [of fate] to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find wide open. "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant."﴾ [al-Isra': 13-14]. As for His saying, ﴿And that is easy for Allah﴾, the demonstrative refers back to the resurrection, and its ease is an established matter, because restoration is easier than initiation, as Allah the Exalted said about the disbelievers: ﴿And he presents for Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78-79]; and His saying: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are but as [that of] a single soul﴾ [Luqman: 28]; and He said: ﴿And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the light which We have sent down﴾.

Here, "the light" refers to the Qur'an, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. It is the Qur'an. The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, had already discussed it at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He it is who sends down upon His servant clear verses﴾ [al-Hadid: 9], in the surah "al-Hadid". In al-Mudhakkira, he named it light because it dispels (p-201) the darkness of ignorance, doubt, polytheism, and hypocrisy.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 64, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering﴾.

The Day of Gathering is the Day of Resurrection. The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) said: it is an adverbial object (zarf manṣūb) governed by an implied "udhkur" (remember), or by His saying: ﴿is All-Aware﴾ [at-Taghabun: 8].

So the meaning is: that Day, the Day of Resurrection, is All-Aware of your deeds in the world, nothing of them being hidden from Him, so that He will recompense you for them. It is called the Day of Gathering because the first and the last are gathered in it onto one level plain; the caller makes them hear, and the sight reaches them all, as He, exalted, said: ﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter will surely be gathered for the appointed time of a known Day﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 49–50].

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) has already discussed this in several places, among them in the third volume at His saying, exalted: ﴿That is a Day on which mankind will be gathered﴾ [Hud: 103].

Among them also in the seventh volume at the verse already cited: ﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter will surely be gathered﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 49–50].

Among the clearest evidences for it is the verse of ash-Shura: ﴿and warn of the Day of Gathering, about which there is no doubt﴾, then He said: ﴿a group in the Garden and a group in the Blaze﴾ [ash-Shura: 7].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾.

Al-ghabn (loss) is the feeling of deficiency. Its counterpart is al-khabn, since the two share two of their three letters, as stated in Fiqh al-Lughah. There is a closeness in meaning between them, like the closeness of the differing letters, which are ghayn and khā'. Because the ghayn is hidden in the throat while the khā' is manifest from it, al-ghabn is for what is hidden and al-khabn is for what is manifest.

Allah, exalted, has explained what causes ghabn for the one who gains and the one who loses, saying: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement﴾ [at-Taghabun: 9]. He explained the state of the one who loses by His saying: ﴿But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs — those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever, and wretched is the destination﴾ [at-Taghabun: 10].

The scholars have explained the reality of ghabn in this context: every person has a place in Paradise and a place in the Fire. When the people of the Fire enter the Fire, their places in Paradise remain; and when the people of Paradise enter Paradise, their places in the Fire remain.

There, the dwellings of the people of Paradise in the Fire become for the people of the Fire, and the dwellings of the people of the Fire in Paradise become for the people of Paradise, who inherit them from them. Thus there is the painful loss, which is the exchange of a place in the Fire for a place in Paradise, since they inherited the places of the others who went to the Fire.

﴿Not a misfortune strikes except by the permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah, He will guide his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

In this noble verse there is a clear text that no misfortune befalls anyone except by the permission of Allah.

It is well known that likewise no good befalls anyone except by the permission of Allah, in the same manner as His saying: ﴿And He made for you garments to protect you from the heat﴾ [An-Nahl: 81], meaning and [from] the cold.

However, the specific mention of misfortune here is to indicate that everything that reaches the servant is only by the permission of Allah, because human nature dislikes misfortunes and seeks to avoid them, yet they still reach him, and he has no power to repel them. This differs from good, which a person may claim he obtained through his own effort, as Qarun said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I have﴾ [Al-Qasas: 78].

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah, He will guide his heart﴾, it has been read as (yahda') with a hamza, from al-huduw (calm), and (qalbuhu) with a damma (nominative), and it means "yahdi qalbahu" (He guides his heart). This is because he knows that what afflicted him would not have missed him, so he says "inna lillah" and his heart is at rest through this and he does not panic. This is one of the characteristics of the believer.

As the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer: if good befalls him, he gives thanks, and that is good for him; and if harm befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him. Even the thorn that pricks his foot [is good for him]."

Similar to this is His saying: ﴿And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits. But give good tidings to the patient, who, when disaster strikes them, say, "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return." Those upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and those are the [rightly] guided﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 155–157].

That is: [they are guided] to what is incumbent upon them of obedience and patience. For this reason, after it came: ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾ [At-Taghabun: 12].

(p-203) From another aspect it is said: His saying ﴿Not a misfortune strikes except by the permission of Allah﴾ — and disbelief is the greatest of misfortunes — and ﴿whoever believes in Allah, He will guide his heart﴾ — and belief in Allah is the greatest of blessings. So a speaker may say: If all of that is by the permission of Allah, then what is the sin of the disbeliever and what is the virtue of the believer? Thus came His saying: ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾, clarifying what is incumbent upon the servant, which is obedience to the Messengers in what they brought, and he has no power over anything other than that.

In His saying ﴿He will guide his heart﴾, the attribution of guidance to the heart is an explanation of the matter of general and specific guidance. The scholars said the same regarding His saying concerning the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [Ash-Shura: 52], alongside His saying: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [Al-Qasas: 56].

They said: the first guidance is guidance of indication (dalalat irshad), like His saying: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17].

The second is guidance of divine enabling (tawfiq) and direction, and what supports this is the resemblance of the guidance from Allah to the heart of whoever believes in Allah. And His saying ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾, by repeating the verb "obey," indicates that obedience to the Messenger is binding in its own right.

The Sunnah has come with independent legislations and with specifying the Qur'an and the like, as was mentioned earlier at His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾ [Al-Hashr: 7].

What witnesses to this is His saying: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾ [An-Nisa': 59]. He repeated the verb with respect to Allah and the Messenger, but did not repeat it with respect to those in authority, because their obedience is not independent but follows the obedience to Allah and the obedience to His Messenger, as in the hadith: "There is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 64, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them﴾.

The discussion of this was previously given by the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon him and upon us) at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Wealth and children are the adornment of the worldly life﴾ (p. 204) [al-Kahf: 46].

Among what is considered a Qur'anic guidance for treating the problems of married life and the matter of children is the sequel to this in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Taghabun: 14]. That is: the enmity of spouses and children should not be met except with pardon, forbearance and forgiveness, and that this lightens, removes, or keeps away from the spouse and the parent the consequences of this enmity, and that it is better than contention and quarrelling.

In another place He said: ﴿Indeed, your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ [al-Taghabun: 15], that is: they may divert you from the remembrance of Allah: ﴿Let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9].

The Shaykh had previously treated this topic in Surah "al-Kahf," as we have pointed out.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 64, verse 16:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So fear God as much as you are able﴾.

It is understood from this that the obligation is within the limits of capacity. This is clarified by His words: ﴿God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286].

And His words: ﴿Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286].

In the hadith: "God said: 'I have done it'," and this applies to commands, not prohibitions, because prohibitions are abstentions (turuk).

As came in the Sunnah: "What I have commanded you, do as much of it as you are able; and what I have forbidden you, avoid it." This is one of the distinctive features of this Ummah.

As the Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him, previously mentioned at the end of surah al-Baqarah, and its verification applies to the concessions (rukhas) regarding prayer, fasting and similar matters.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess (shuḥḥ) of his soul, those are the successful﴾.

They said: shuḥḥ is more specific than bukhl (miserliness). It was also said: bukhl is that you withhold your own wealth, while shuḥḥ is that you withhold the wealth of others. The reality is that shuḥḥ is the extreme of bukhl. Its mention here, after the matters of spouses and children, their trials and their enmity, and then the command to listen, obey and spend in His words: ﴿Listen, obey, and spend; it is better for yourselves﴾ [al-Taghabun: 16], indicates that most matters of marriage originate from the side of wealth, either through greed for it, by striving to obtain it on their account, which may lead to temptation through it, or through stinginess with it after obtaining it, which may lead to their enmity over it.

The effective remedy for all of this is spending and guarding against shuḥḥ. Shuḥḥ is part of the innate nature of the soul: ﴿And souls have been present with stinginess﴾ [al-Nisa': 128]. In the attribution of shuḥḥ to the soul (nafs), together with the attribution of guidance earlier to the heart (qalb), there is a subtle secret: shuḥḥ is the natural disposition of humankind, while guidance is a divine gift; the former is an animal power, and the latter is a spiritual power.

Therefore the Muslim must overcome the innate human power with the spiritual power, so that he may attain success and triumph, as God indicated in His words: ﴿Wealth and children are the adornment of the worldly life﴾. Then He said: ﴿But the lasting good deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in hope﴾ [al-Kahf: 46].

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Listen and obey﴾.

That is: do not be like those who said, "We hear and we disobey," nor like the people of Noah, about whom He said: ﴿And indeed, every time I have called them, that You may forgive them, they have put their fingers into their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and grown arrogant with extreme arrogance﴾ [Nuh: 7].

He also condemned the words of the disbelievers: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it﴾ [Fussilat: 26].

The Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him, said: Listen to what is said to you, and obey in what you have heard, not like those before you who were referred to by the preceding verses.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-418) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Taghabun

The words of the Exalted ﴿So fear God as much as you are able﴾. The apparent contradiction between it and His words ﴿Fear God as He should be feared﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102] has already been resolved in surat Al 'Imran.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 64, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you lend to Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allah is Most Appreciative, Forbearing.﴾

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) said: Allah, exalted is He, has made clear that He multiplies the spending to seven hundred and more, by His saying: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 261].

The root meaning of qard (loan) in the language is "cutting off", and in the Sharia it is the cutting off of a portion of wealth which one gives to someone who benefits from it, and then he returns it. That is, Allah, exalted is He, returns it multiplied. He has named His dealing with His servants a loan, a sale, a purchase and a trade.

The meaning of all of this is that the servant acts for the sake of Allah's Face, and Allah, Majestic and Exalted, gives him the reward of that deed, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you lend to Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you﴾, to the end of the verse [at-Taghabun: 17].

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, [giving them] Paradise in return﴾ [at-Tawbah: 111].

And His saying: ﴿So rejoice in your transaction which you have conducted﴾ [at-Tawbah: 111].

And His saying: ﴿Shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? [It is that] you believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth﴾, to the end of the verse [as-Saff: 10-11], along with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿a trade that will never perish﴾ [Fatir: 29].

The goodly loan is that which comes from lawful earnings, sincerely for the sake of Allah. End of quotation.

Among what bears witness to his saying, may Allah have mercy on him, regarding the meaning of the goodly loan, is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 264]; because such a person has not spent sincerely for the sake of Allah's Face. The mention of "goodly" with the goodly loan here, after the matter of marriage, children, and guarding against stinginess, indicates that spending on children and wife is in fact a form of goodly loan with Allah, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: Whatever good you spend is for parents and relatives﴾ [al-Baqarah: 215].

The nearest of the relatives after the parents are the children and the wife.

And in the hadith encouraging spending: "Even the morsel that a man places into his wife's mouth."

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is Most Appreciative, Forbearing﴾ [at-Taghabun: 17].

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) said: Allah's appreciation of His servant is His rewarding him with a great reward for a small deed.

As for His saying "Forbearing", it means He does not hasten to punish, but rather He covers over and overlooks sins. The mention of this concluding phrase here indicates guidance in some aspects of family reform: that each spouse should receive the other's action with gratitude, and meet every offense with forbearance, so that the meaning of good companionship is fulfilled; and because spending deserves to be met with gratitude, while enmity is met with forbearance.

(p-207) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾.

The verse coming with a nominal sentence (al-jumla al-ismiyya) indicates restriction (al-hasr), and He has stated this explicitly in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. Its coming here also indicates that the watch over the family between the two parties belongs only to Allah, may He be exalted, because they are in seclusion from people, and none has knowledge of what lies between them except Allah, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. That is: let each of them be mindful of his Lord, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and (know that He is) the one who recompenses each of them for his action.
